name: bleeding patient overview
title: Bleeding patient decision chart: stabilize first and transfuse only the missing component, then the site of bleeding splits a platelet-type (primary hemostasis) problem from a coagulation-factor (secondary) problem; the platelet count, bleeding score and von Willebrand screen sort von Willebrand disease from platelet function disorders, and an isolated long aPTT points to hemophilia; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment

root.title: Bleeding patient: STABILIZE, then is it a PLATELET problem or a FACTOR problem?
lines: 1 · ABCs  ·  2 · find and stop the source; transfuse ONLY what is missing  ·  3 · work up the cause

transfuse: red cells if hemoglobin (Hb) < 70 g/L (70–90 with coronary disease) · platelets < 10, < 50 for surgery, < 100 for neurosurgery · MASSIVE bleeding → massive transfusion protocol + early fibrinogen + tranexamic acid
first tests: complete blood count (CBC) + film · prothrombin time (PT/INR) · activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) ± thrombin time · fibrinogen · liver + kidney function
serious bleeding or trauma: treat first, investigate later

groups.title: MUCOSAL, SKIN: PRIMARY hemostasis (platelets, von Willebrand factor (vWF), vessels)
lines: petechiae < 2 mm, purpura, bruising · nose, gums, heavy menses · bleeds at once
NORMAL PT + aPTT do NOT exclude it

tiers.title: Platelet COUNT normal (LOW → THROMBOCYTOPENIA chart)
lines: • bleeding assessment tool (ISTH BAT) abnormal: ≥ 4 men, ≥ 6 women, ≥ 3 children

tiers.title: aPTT LONG, PT/INR NORMAL
lines: any other pattern → ADULT COAGULOPATHY chart
